paper_title: Stronger limits on hypothetical Yukawa interactions in the 40--8000 nm range
suggested_experiment_name: Riverside (this work) — Yukawa force search via differential force measurement with Casimir subtraction
coupling_convention: α (dimensionless coupling strength relative to gravity), as plotted on y-axis of Fig. 4
notes: Paper reports new differential force measurements searching for Yukawa-like corrections to Newtonian gravity in the λ ∈ [30–8000 nm] range. The coupling parameter α is the dimensionless strength of a putative Yukawa interaction V(r) = −Gm₁m₂/r · α·exp(−r/λ) relative to gravity. The paper establishes 95% confidence level exclusion limits shown in Fig. 4 (red curve). Data points extracted from the boundary of the excluded region: at λ ≈ 30 nm, α ≲ 10⁻³; at λ ≈ 8000 nm, α ≲ 10⁻⁷. The coupling type is ScalarNucleon because the experiment constrains a Yukawa-type fifth force between nucleons via differential measurements of materials with different densities (Au vs Si), which probes scalar coupling to nucleon mass. The technique subtracts the Casimir force background and uses a rotating source mass with lock-in detection to achieve improvements up to 10³ over previous limits. Confidence is moderate (0.75) because while the experimental method and mass range are clear, the exact numerical values are read from a figure rather than provided in tabular form, and the paper's primary focus is on the experimental technique rather than dark matter or ultralight boson searches per se. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 54)) | Vision: The exclusion plot (FIG. 4) shows the λ-α phase space where λ is the range (in meters) of a hypothetical Yukawa-like force and α is its coupling strength relative to gravity. The x-axis spans 40 nm to 8000 nm (1e-7 to 1e-3 m), corresponding to mass range via m = ℏc/λ. Conversion: m[eV] = 1.240e-6 eV·m / λ[m]. The red curve labeled 'Riverside' represents the new limits from this work. The region ABOVE the red curve is excluded by the experiment. The y-axis shows α on a log scale from 1e-9 to 1e-5. The coupling type is ScalarNucleon because the paper searches for Yukawa-like fifth forces between nucleons via differential force measurements. The data points trace the lower boundary of the exclusion region (the red curve) from shortest to longest range (highest to lowest mass).
